originalBehavior: The route should remain a longform Engineering Sandbox article with a shared hero, generated story rail, and local provenance handling.
localStatus: The route still uses the shared Engineering Sandbox shell while keeping all public teaching content local to the Formula 1 route.
notes: The shell provides the longform wrapper and generated chapter navigation.
Public provenance remains neutral because the route is an original local build.
evidence: The route hero, generated chapter rail, and mobile chapter navigation are mounted by the shared shell.
The public route still uses neutral provenance handling rather than an upstream reference page.

originalBehavior: The route should use the Bartosz-family base runtime for shared controls and math utilities, with the file kept unmodified.
localStatus: The route now ships a local copy of base.js and base.css so sliders, segmented controls, touch handlers, ArcBall rotation, and shared math helpers are available inside the Formula 1 route itself.
notes: The local base runtime is intended to stay unmodified unless the route explicitly forks that engine.
The Formula 1 route uses the runtime directly rather than only imitating its control patterns.
evidence: The route head now loads ./js/base.js and ./css/base.css before the route-specific runtime.
The overview scene uses ArcBall rotation and the route controls use Slider and SegmentedControl instances from the base runtime.

originalBehavior: The route should feel closer to the Bartosz family by drawing key scenes procedurally instead of relying on static infographic panels.
localStatus: The route now renders the overview, airflow, front-wing, floor, rear-wing, chassis, power, tyre, braking, track, racecraft, setup, weather, pit, and lap scenes procedurally on canvas, with the overview and aero chapters pushed toward fuller pseudo-3D geometry.
notes: The drawings are explanatory and stylized rather than scan-based or model-import-based.
The route uses procedural silhouettes, animated flow lines, shaded bands, and dynamic traces to make the scenes feel more alive.
Recent updates increased the depth and lighting of the overview and aero chapters so they read less like flat dashboards and more like procedural pseudo-3D scenes.
evidence: Each chapter scene mounts through a drawer_container instead of static metric-card dashboards.
The route runtime draws and repaints scene state directly on canvas in response to base-runtime controls.

originalBehavior: Track, setup, floor posture, power, tyre, and weather decisions should connect back into a shared lap-time story rather than living as isolated widgets.
localStatus: The route keeps a shared Formula 1 state model so track presets, setup sliders, live floor posture, tyre choice, power maps, and weather propagate into the lap-builder scene and chapter summaries.
notes: Track presets change setup, tyre, power, and lap-plan defaults together.
The live floor controls model the platform during the lap while setup ride height remains the selected baseline.
Pit timing remains a separate race-strategy calculation because the final scene models one lap rather than a stint or race.
evidence: Selecting a new track preset updates setup sliders, tyre compound, power mode, power bias, and lap plan together.
Changing live floor ride height or pitch updates floor health, track-weighted sector scores, the speed trace, and the final lap caption.
Weather changes the lap model while pit state remains confined to the pit-strategy scene and caption.

originalBehavior: The Floor and Diffuser chapter should show why platform posture matters and carry that consequence into the final lap rather than ending at a local animation.
localStatus: Named ride-height and pitch controls feed one computeFloorState result for suction, stability, risk, sector loss, trace shape, and the final floor contribution.
notes: Track-specific weights make floor posture matter most on high-speed circuits and sectors.
The result is deliberately explanatory rather than telemetry-grade, CFD-derived, or suspension-simulated.
The next planned depth pass is explicit labeling for the remaining controls, followed by tyre thermal coupling.
evidence: The floor scene and caption consume the same computed health state as the lap model.
The lap canvas labels all three sector deltas and the lap caption identifies the floor-attributed loss.
Focused smoke drives live ride height to its keyboard maximum and verifies changed floor and lap captions, high platform risk, and nonzero floor loss.

originalBehavior: Formula 1 controls change procedural scene state and linked captions through pointer and touch interaction.
localStatus: Shared segmented controls are radio groups with Arrow-key selection, while shared sliders expose slider value semantics and Arrow, Home, and End behavior.
notes: Track, weather, lap-plan, airflow speed, live floor ride height, and floor pitch have stable data-control selectors.
The floor controls also provide visible labels without modifying the shared base runtime.
Reduced-motion preference stops perpetual repainting but repaints scenes after state changes.
evidence: Focused smoke uses keyboard input on track, weather, lap-plan, airflow, and live floor controls and verifies aria state plus linked captions.
The floor keyboard check proves the same input updates both its local explanation and the final lap result.
